generated/rdflib/namespace.py:145-147 (Namespace.__contains__) and generated/rdflib/namespace.py:218-225 (ClosedNamespace.__contains__) match the two namespace hunks in patch.diff; generated/test/test_namespace.py:117-130 matches the test hunk.
Candidate test/test_namespace.py changes are additive (new import line and new class); no existing test is removed or altered in behavior.

The membership operators are added to Namespace (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:145) and ClosedNamespace (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:218), the same classes the reference modifies (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:149 and :223).

_RDFNamespace (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:221-ish region, class at base rdflib/namespace.py:221) inherits from ClosedNamespace, so the logic lives in the owning module rather than in a new location.
Tests are added to the existing module test/test_namespace.py alongside NamespacePrefixTest (base test/test_namespace.py:8).

generated/rdflib/namespace.py:145-147: __contains__(self, ref) returns a bool from str(ref).startswith(str(self)); the signature and bool return match the reference shape (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:149-150).

generated/rdflib/namespace.py:218-225: __contains__ returns any(ref == str(uri) ...) over the stored terms, a bool; the reference uses ref in self.__uris.values() (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:223-224).

Divergence on non-URIRef input: the candidate coerces with str(), so a plain str or Literal whose text equals a term URI is reported as a member (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:224). The reference relies on Identifier.__eq__ type checking (base rdflib/term.py:160-163), which returns False across types. The issue asks about URIRef membership, and URIRef behavior matches, so this is an alternative choice rather than a contract violation. The docstring says 'equals' while the code compares string values, a minor inaccuracy.
The patch adds no import statements to any rdflib module; diff shows only the existing 'from rdflib.namespace import FOAF' line in test/test_namespace.py widened to FOAF, RDF, RDFS, SH, Namespace.
All imported names exist in rdflib/namespace.py (RDF at base:478, RDFS at base:479, SH at base:500, Namespace at base:104), so the test depends only on the library module it exercises.

Membership is provided through Python's __contains__ data-model hook on Namespace (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:145) and ClosedNamespace (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:218); _RDFNamespace (base rdflib/namespace.py:221) inherits it with no extra registration needed.

NamespaceManager: the reference adds a misspelled __contians__ (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:602), which the 'in' operator never calls, so the reference does not actually provide NamespaceManager membership. The base NamespaceManager class (base rdflib/namespace.py:547) defines no __iter__, __getitem__, or __contains__, so 'in' raises TypeError before and after the candidate.
The issue body describes NamespaceManager membership only as a 'possible extension', so omitting it is not a missing requirement and is not a regression.
The patch introduces no new packages or imports; the implementation uses only built-in str and any() (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:147, 225).

Membership logic stays inside the namespace module's classes that own the data. ClosedNamespace reads its own stored mapping (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:225 uses self.__uris) rather than going through term(), so _RDFNamespace's on-the-fly rdf:_n construction (base rdflib/namespace.py:280-292) is not treated as a stored member.
Result matches the reference for rdf:_1: candidate returns False because _1 is not stored; reference behaves the same (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:223-224 over __uris.values()).
The feature uses the language's standard __contains__ protocol (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:145, 218), the same mechanism the reference uses (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:149, 223).
No parallel helper method or new public API is introduced; term() and __getitem__ are left unchanged, which avoids touching existing lookup paths.
The change is a pure membership check inside rdflib/namespace.py; it does not touch term construction, parsers, or serializers.
Existing str-based 'in' checks are unaffected: notation3 uses ':' in ns on plain str values from uriOf (base rdflib/plugins/parsers/notation3.py:597-609, 663), not Namespace objects.
infixowl.ClassNamespaceFactory (base rdflib/extras/infixowl.py:687) subclasses Namespace and inherits the prefix check; it does not use 'in', so its behavior is unchanged.
Naming follows the file: NamespaceContainsTest mirrors the existing NamespacePrefixTest (base test/test_namespace.py:8), and test methods use the test_* unittest pattern with assertTrue/assertFalse.
Docstrings use the module's reST-style triple-quoted form (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:146, 219-223).

Minor nits, not failures: .pep8 sets max-line-length = 85 (base .pep8:3) and several added lines exceed it (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:146 at 91 chars; generated/test/test_namespace.py:119-130 at 92-102 chars), though the base test file already has a 94-char line (base test/test_namespace.py:77). Lines 126 and 130 use assertIs(..., False) where the rest of the file uses assertFalse, a stylistic variance.

Namespace prefix membership: URIRef('http://example.org/Person') in Namespace('http://example.org/') is True, and a URI outside the prefix is False (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:147; generated/test/test_namespace.py:119-121). This matches the issue's goal of replacing manual ref.startswith(ns) with 'ref in ns'.

Closed membership: RDFS.label is True and rdfs:example is False (generated/rdflib/namespace.py:218-225; generated/test/test_namespace.py:125-126). RDF.type is True and rdf:_1 is False (generated/test/test_namespace.py:129-130), matching the reference's behavior for container properties.

Regression check: 'in' on a Namespace changes from str substring semantics to prefix semantics, which is intended and is also done by the reference (reference/rdflib/namespace.py:149-150). 'in' on a ClosedNamespace previously fell back to __getitem__ iteration, which raises KeyError (base rdflib/namespace.py:196-198), so it did not return a membership answer before. The candidate's change therefore does not break any existing working behavior.
Existing tests in the base suite use 'in' only on bytes/str values (base test/test_namespace.py:58, 74), so they are unaffected.
